problem: Existing visual navigation policies (modular or end-to-end RL) need online interaction, maps, depth, poses or exploration to adapt to a new scene, so they cannot adapt to a novel environment from a passive traversal video alone.
motivation: Humans can navigate an unfamiliar space after watching a short walkthrough video, relying only on visual recognition and memory. The paper asks whether a policy can be learned purely offline from egocentric RGB videos and then adapt to new scenes by taking a context video as input, with no finetuning.
key_idea: Label actions in egocentric context videos with optical flow (pseudo action labeling), then train an in-context bidirectional recurrent Transformer with offline RL (BCQ) and a temporal coherence loss, so it navigates to goal images in new scenes given only a new context video.
insight: The context video carries real navigational information: removing it (NOLO-C) drops SR from 43.65 to 33.58 on Habitat and from 71.20 to 67.78 on RoboTHOR. The temporal coherence loss matters more in the larger Habitat scenes (NOLO-T 37.48 SR vs 43.65) and gives better structured t-SNE embeddings. The pseudo-action quality also matters: replacing GMFlow (92.44% action accuracy) with SuperGlue matching (80.43%) cuts SR by about 5-7 points, so the framework is only as good as its action decoder.
method: Pseudo action labeling: GMFlow optical flow between adjacent frames, filtered to the top-decile dominant vectors, then threshold rules on horizontal/vertical displacement (tau_x, tau_y) discretize into turn vs forward actions, turning RGB videos into frame-action trajectories

Bidirectional recurrent Transformer policy (VN-Bert): ResNet18 (Places365) frame encoder, action embedding, and a frozen CLIP goal-image encoder. Nine self-attention BERT layers encode the context trajectory plus a hidden state. Four LXMERT cross-attention layers combine the fixed context, current observation and goal with a recurrent hidden state, initialized from PREVALENT
Heads and losses: action distribution (cross-entropy on pseudo-actions), Q-value head, and a termination head trained on d_t = I(o_t = g)
Batch-Constrained Q-learning: binary goal-reaching reward and Bellman update restricted to actions whose probability ratio to the max exceeds beta=0.5, which suits suboptimal rule-based videos

Temporal coherence loss: a temporal indicator (1D self-attention with spectral norm) is trained with a Bradley-Terry preference loss so later frames score higher than earlier ones, aligning visual embeddings with temporal order

Semantic actions and inference: the policy outputs (action, duration) pairs with duration up to 3 steps; actions are chosen by Q-values weighted by the masked policy (epsilon=0.999), and STOP is output when the termination head is confident

Data: a non-exploratory rule-based policy (forward until collision, then random turn) records a 900-step (~30 s) RGB video per scene; Detic finds the objects, and goal images are rolled out from various views

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (Places365) + frozen CLIP-RN50 goal encoder + 9-layer BERT self-attention and 4-layer LXMERT cross-attention Transformer (initialized from PREVALENT, trained with BCQ)
setting.training_data: Rule-based egocentric RGB videos, one 900-step video per scene with GMFlow pseudo-action labels: 48 RoboTHOR scenes (12 rooms x 4 layouts) or 70 Matterport3D scenes in Habitat; no extra web data
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB 224x224 (plus a context video and a goal image); no depth, pose or GPS
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveForward 0.25 m, TurnLeft/TurnRight 30°, STOP, with repetition up to 3 (semantic actions)
setting.simulator: RoboTHOR (AI2-THOR) and Habitat (Matterport3D); real Unitree Go2 maze
setting.privileged: none at test time (only a context video of the new scene and a goal image); goal images are taken from the scene

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks (RoboTHOR/Habitat video navigation), not standard leaderboards. The ablation table (Table 2) gives averaged NOLO variants; the main table has different aggregation for RoboTHOR (Table 2 averages both sets: NOLO 71.20 SR / 28.50 SPL; NOLO-C 67.78; NOLO-T 69.03; NOLO(M) 66.15). Habitat: NOLO-C 33.58, NOLO-T 37.48, NOLO(M) 36.73 SR. Real-robot results are qualitative only. Cross-domain results are also shown in a figure.
results: NOLO reaches 71.92 SR / 29.26 SPL (unseen layout) and 70.48 / 27.74 (unseen room) on RoboTHOR, versus 47.04 SR (VGM) and 40.51 SR (VGM) for the strongest baseline, and 43.65 SR / 20.77 SPL on Habitat versus 35.16 (GPT-4o). Cross-domain transfer between RoboTHOR and Habitat stays competitive, and real-world deployment on the Unitree Go2 works from a 600-step context video.
limitations: Actions are decoded from only two adjacent frames, so only simple movements (forward/turn) can be recovered; more complex actions are not handled
Performance drops in large multi-room, multi-floor Habitat scenes (43.65 SR) and the SPL stays low (about 20-29%)
Evaluation is on self-built benchmarks with a single context video per scene; the real-world test is a small maze with only qualitative results
